probeEvidence.notes: Verified live: drag on the compass moved the real panner and bearing read '67 deg right', ArrowRight stepped to 82 deg, Space fired the Capture cue, tab order is field > Play > six tabs > wrap. All six lab states render designed screens with recovery actions. Text scale reflows the whole surface at 1.3/1.75/3.0 with progressive shedding and zero clipping. Outdoor world keeps every line legible via per-text shadows. DEFECT FOUND: after a pointer drag, browser text selection paints a blue highlight over the 'front' rose word (visible in stage-playing.png) - the field lacks user-select:none and pointerdown does not preventDefault. Zero console errors across 12 loads.

blind.A: visionOS Settings > Sounds pane + AirPods spatial-audio personalization head diagram
blind.B: Horizon OS (Quest 3) Settings > System Sounds flat panel

blindDescriptions.A: A floating frosted-glass window over the room. Large white SF Pro heading, rows of settings with blue-accented sliders and toggles, a subtle gaze highlight that follows the eye. The spatial-audio personalization surface shows a centred animated head-with-earbuds illustration on glass with one blue pill action. Strengths: material is true glass, gaze focus is unmistakable, type is flawless. Weaknesses: the sounds pane is a long scroll with weak glanceability at arm's length, loading is a bare spinner, error dialogs are verbose.
blindDescriptions.B: A flat, near-opaque dark grey panel docked in the void. Left section rail, dense toggle rows, small type, no spatial or sound visualization whatsoever - haptics have no system surface at all. Strengths: utilitarian glanceability per row, one column, never ambiguous. Weaknesses: panels read as opaque screens floating nowhere, motion is linear fades and teleports, edge states are generic spinners and toasts, zero delight.
blindDescriptions.C: A head-centred compass disc over a street scrim: one glowing orb orbiting at the cue's bearing, cardinal words outside the rim, a live bearing sentence below, a haptic waveform strip whose bar widths are real milliseconds and heights real intensities, one Play action, six-cue tab strip. Six designed states (loading, autoplay-blocked, no output, no motor, offline) each with a recovery action. Mono and tactile-only modes restructure meaning instead of degrading it. Dragging the orb moves a real HRTF panner live.

referenceScreens.visionOS: Settings > Sounds, plus the AirPods 'spatialize stereo / personalize spatial audio' surface: a single frosted window floating over the wearer's room, SF Pro white text on glass, blue-filled pill controls, a centred head illustration that animates sound placement around the ears, back chevron top-left, and a subtle gaze highlight that brightens the row under the eye. Loading inside these panes is a bare spinner in glass; errors are multi-sentence modal dialogs.
referenceScreens.horizonOS: Quest 3 Settings > System Sounds: a flat near-black rectangle docked in the headset void - no transparency, no world bleed through the panel - with a left rail of sections, small grey labels and toggle switches, and at most one accent color. There is no spatial-audio visualization and no system haptics surface; controller haptics are configured per-app. Motion between panes is a hard swap with a linear fade.

biggestGap: Drag selection glitch · components/17-audio-haptics/index.html:628 (.field pointerdown) · expected: dragging the compass (the signature interaction) paints nothing but the spoke; got: browser text selection highlights the 'front' rose word in blue, visible in reviews/17-audio-haptics/judge-r3/stage-playing.png. Fix: add user-select:none (-webkit-user-select:none) to .field and e.preventDefault() in the pointerdown handler. Secondary: focus discipline is 7 vs visionOS 8 because two bright blue elements glow at rest (the orb and the Play pill); demote the resting Play pill or the bearing dot so exactly one accent leads.
reason: Blind scoring ranked System C first at 75/90 against visionOS 70 and Horizon OS 48. C wins glanceability (orb position plus a plain-language bearing sentence is readable in under a second; visionOS's sounds pane is a scroll of rows), edge states (six designed states each naming what still works and offering recovery - beats visionOS's bare spinner and verbose dialogs), accessibility (mono bus with explicit channel count, spoken direction, tactile-only mode, whole-surface reflow at 300% with nothing clipped, reduced motion verified with zero infinite animations), and delight (the drag-the-sound-around-your-head HRTF demo is a signature moment that serves function). visionOS keeps material honesty (true glass, 9 vs 8) and focus discipline (one gaze-highlighted target; 8 vs 7 where two blue elements glow at rest). Horizon OS's opaque panels, linear motion and generic errors leave it far behind. One concrete defect found and named; the pass condition - ours ranked first overall - is met.
passCondition: Ours ranked first overall (75 vs 70 vs 48). One named gap (drag text-selection glitch) plus two criteria lost to visionOS (focus discipline, material honesty); pass holds because first overall is achieved.
